description: termination_notice_band (D-68, D-158 corrected): the BCEA default and the domestic sector's SD7 override, carried over unchanged from termination_rule_set's retired notice_weeks_* columns; SD1's own two-band notice regime, clause 23(1); and per-boundary inclusivity read from each statute's own wording rather than a single global convention. NOT verified.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s37(1)(a)
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. 's37(1)(a): one week, if the employee has been employed for six months or less'. Upper boundary INCLUSIVE — the statute's own words put exactly six months here, not in band 2. service_from/service_to touch the adjacent band exactly, in the same unit both sides, by construction — the reconciliation check in statutory/checks.py relies on that rather than converting between units.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s37(1)(b)
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. 's37(1)(b): two weeks, if employed for more than six months but not more than one year'. Both boundaries EXCLUSIVE: six months belongs to band 1 ('or less'), and one year belongs to band 3 below — see that band's own note on the genuine overlap in the Act's text at exactly one year (O-06).

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997, s37(1)(c)(i)
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. 's37(1)(c)(i): four weeks, if the employee has been employed for one year or more'. GENUINE OVERLAP IN THE ACT (O-06): s37(1)(b) says 'not more than one year' and this clause says 'one year or more' — both name exactly one year of service. Four weeks (the richer entitlement) is the reading loaded here, not a reading of what the boundary itself unambiguously says, because there is no such single reading — flagged for the labour law review rather than asserted as settled.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 7: Domestic Worker Sector, published in Regulation Gazette No. 7434 (consolidated text), read with Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997 s37(1)(c); SD7 clause 24(1)(a)
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. Upper boundary INCLUSIVE, same reading as the BCEA default's own band 1 — six months or less is one week regardless of sector. service_from/service_to touch the adjacent band exactly, in the same unit both sides, by construction — the reconciliation check in statutory/checks.py relies on that rather than converting between units.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 7: Domestic Worker Sector, published in Regulation Gazette No. 7434 (consolidated text), read with Basic Conditions of Employment Act 75 of 1997 s37(1)(c); SD7 clause 24(1)(b)
termination_notice_band.notes: Carried over from termination_rule_set.notice_weeks_* (D-68) — the same figure, the same citation, now with its own unit instead of an implied week. BCEA s37(1)(c)(ii): four weeks for a domestic worker employed for MORE THAN six months — exclusive, unlike the ordinary s37(1)(c)(i) one-year mark, because this clause states its own threshold at six months with no companion clause contesting it. SD7's 6-months-and-over and over-1-year columns held the same figure (4 weeks), so this is one open-ended band rather than a redundant third one with no real boundary.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 1: Contract Cleaning Sector, current consolidated text (clauses 3, 8-24), clause 23(1)(a)
termination_notice_band.notes: 'during the first four weeks of employment, not less than one working day's [notice]'. A DAY, not a fraction of a week — see the model docstring. Upper boundary INCLUSIVE: 'the first four weeks' names exactly four weeks as still inside it. service_from/service_to touch the adjacent band exactly, in the same unit both sides, by construction — the reconciliation check in statutory/checks.py relies on that rather than converting between units.

termination_notice_band.source_reference: Sectoral Determination 1: Contract Cleaning Sector, current consolidated text (clauses 3, 8-24), clause 23(1)(b)
termination_notice_band.notes: 'four weeks, if the employee has been employed for more than four weeks'. EXCLUSIVE lower boundary: 'more than four weeks' is the Act's own word for it, and band 1 above already holds exactly four weeks inclusively (D-158, corrected — the first version of this fixture had this the other way round).
